labels.label: thm:lower-bound
labels.what_is_proved: Over the measured model (DEC-186), under thm:upper-bound's hypotheses read as the strict upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos reads them, and thm:main's hypotheses (MeanPoincare, TraceBound, InteriorBump, eq:star with any constant Ã): R_g ≡ c < 0 and EH(Σ,g) = Y_[g](Σ); κF_g(1) > 0; δ(Σ,g) ≥ F_g(1)/Λ_max (eq:main's form) and δ(Σ,g) ≥ κF_g(1) (eq:lower-bound) for every value σb ≥ 0 of σ^∂(Σ); |R_g| Vol^{2/N} ≥ κF_g(1) (eq:R-bound before the dilute limit, no σ^∂ needed); for round B_j of radii r_j, F_g(1) = 2(N−1)M/Vol^{(N−2)/N} and |R_g| ≥ κ·2(N−1)M/Vol; the remainder of eq:kappa is the explicit mainRem N θ Ã F, O(F²) at fixed θ, Ã, with |mainRem| ≤ (5/7)(ÃF/a_N)² for |ÃF/a_N| ≤ 1/4 uniformly in θ. Both forms of thm:main are covered (thm_lower_bound: eq:star for u ≥ 0 + AbsLatticeApprox; thm_lower_bound_signed: eq:star for every u), so OQ-111 (a) picks one with no Lean change. Instances: N = 3 at star3AtilCorr V λ C (corrected thm:star3), N ≥ 3 at starNAtil (prop:starN), for any valid λ, C. On a model reading a compact connected manifold with boundary (Mfd.Reads, OQ-93) at λ₁ and C_SP of def:constants: MeanPoincare, the trace theorem, λ₁ ∈ (0,∞), C_SP < ∞ and eq:star are discharged. lem:positivity (and R_g ≤ 0) is not carried: inf F_g ≥ F_g(1)/Λ_max > 0 comes from thm:main. Witness: toy_thm_lower_bound discharges every hypothesis on the two-point toy model (R_g ≡ −8, σb = 0) and gets a positive bound.

findings: Missing hypothesis (thm:lower-bound l.514–524; eq:gap-bdry l.352–353; eq:sigma-torus l.366–369; companion perforated.tex l.924–925). thm:lower-bound states δ(Σ,g) ≥ κF_g(1) under thm:upper-bound's hypotheses alone, with δ = σ^∂(Σ) − EH(Σ,g). The proof it points to (l.538; the companion: « δ ≥ λ_∂ whenever Yb(Σ) ≥ 0 », l.925) needs σ^∂(Σ) ≥ 0. thm:upper-bound's hypotheses (σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0, l.495) do not give it, and the paper proves it for no Σ̄: for Σ̄ = T³ it is eq:sigma-torus, whose lower half (« attaching Schwarzschild collars of mass tending to zero », l.369) is argued; for any other Σ̄ with σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0 the sign of σ^∂(Σ) is not discussed. Without a sign the argument gives δ(Σ,g) ≥ σ^∂(Σ) + κF_g(1), and −EH(Σ,g) ≥ κF_g(1) (Lean: Yamabe.MeasuredModel.gap_ge_of_le_infF). The printed bound is proved with σ^∂(Σ) ≥ 0 carried (hσb in every thm_lower_bound*). No counterexample is formalized: σ^∂(Σ) is a supremum over conformal classes and cannot be defined on the model. Suggested fix: add « and σ^∂(Σ) ≥ 0 » to the theorem (as the companion does at l.925), or state it for Σ̄ = T³ and prove eq:sigma-torus.

Minor, the second equality of eq:lower-bound (l.522–524). « κF_g(1) = κ·2(N−1)M/Vol^{(N−2)/N} » is eq:F1-torus (l.469), stated for Schwarzschild-like punctured metrics, whose B_j are round spheres of radius r_j (the Setting, l.467). thm:lower-bound assumes only thm:upper-bound's hypotheses, under which each B_j is only conformally round. Then M (eq:mass-def l.385, def:reference l.379–380) is defined only for B_j of positive Gauss curvature (N = 3). Minkowski's inequality ∫_{∂C}H ≥ √(4π|∂C|), with equality only for a round sphere, gives c_3|B_j|^{1/2} ≤ 4M_j, hence F_g(1) ≤ 4M/Vol^{1/3}, strictly when some B_j is not round. There the equality is false, and the M form of the bound does not follow from the F form. This is argued, not formalized. Lean states the M forms as conjuncts conditional on round areas (through Yamabe.MeasuredModel.Fq_one_round). Suggested fix: « for a Schwarzschild-like punctured g » before the second equality.

Minor, wording (l.530). « Ã depends only on the Sobolev–Poincaré and Poincaré constants of (Σ,g) »: the constants actually proved depend on Vol(Σ,g) as well, both the corrected thm:star3's star3AtilCorr V λ₁ C_SP and prop:starN's starNAtil q c_q V λ₁ C_SP (companion eq:Atil l.606–618, where V enters G). λ₁ is not scale-invariant and Ã is, so V enters through λ₁V^{2/N}. Suggested wording: « … constants and the volume of (Σ,g) ».

Minor, the optimality clause (l.530). « The factor θ/(1+θ) is optimal » is the companion's thm:sharp (perforated l.211), which is about λ_∂ = inf F_g. The bound on δ passes through the one-sided δ ≥ λ_∂ (thm:upper-bound; perforated l.925). Optimality of θ/(1+θ) for δ would also need δ ≤ λ_∂(1 + o(1)), and neither paper states or proves that: eq:sandwich (l.547) gives only δ ≤ F_g(1). Not formalized (T-perf-dilute-limit).

Remark, a simplification (l.530–535). eq:R-bound does not need σ^∂(Σ). |R_g|Vol^{2/N} = −Y_[g](Σ) ≥ λ_∂ ≥ κF_g(1) follows from thm:upper-bound and thm:main directly, without δ: R_g < 0 and EH = Y are derived, and the σ-free core is proved as the conjunct κF_g(1) ≤ |c|Vol^{2/N}. So the « giving » at l.530 holds even where finding 1's hypothesis fails. The companion's cor:yamabe writes |R_g|Vol^{2/N} = δ (perforated l.934), which needs Yb(Σ) = 0.
questions: σ^∂(Σ) ≥ 0 (finding 1): is it a hypothesis of thm:lower-bound, or is the theorem meant for Σ̄ = T³ only, with eq:sigma-torus as a lemma to prove? Reading taken: a carried hypothesis 0 ≤ σb, every statement quantified over the value σb of σ^∂(Σ); the sign-free form δ ≥ σ^∂ + κF_g(1) is proved too.

« (area-weighted) mean over ∂Σ » (l.514) against the companion's weights w_j = |B_j|^{(N−2)/(N−1)}/S (perforated l.156–170, eq:ell), which lem:holder (l.479) shows to be the optimal ones. They agree only for n = 1 or equal areas. Reading taken: the companion's (MeasuredModel.capStar, ell); with literal area weights the second identity of eq:calib (c_N/C_2² = F_g(1), perforated l.512) fails for n ≥ 2 with unequal areas, since lem:holder's minimum 1/S is attained only at the companion's weights, so the proof as printed would not give θ/(1+θ) for that θ.

Which form of thm:main is of record (OQ-111 (a)) and the reading of O(F_g(1)²) (OQ-111 (b)): both forms are stated (thm_lower_bound, thm_lower_bound_signed) with the explicit remainder mainRem; no Lean change is needed for either answer.

Which Ã instantiates « explicit κ »: the statement holds for every Ã with eq:star; N = 3 at star3AtilCorr (OQ-109's correction), N ≥ 3 at starNAtil (OQ-118, any lem:elem constant c_q on the model, c_q = q²2^q on the manifold form). OQ-109 and OQ-118 choose an instance and do not touch the statement.

« δ » in the companion (perforated l.924) is Yb(Σ) − Y_[g](Σ), « Yb » being « the supremum over conformal classes of the boundary Yamabe energy » (l.916), which could also be read as the boundary-normalized EHB. Reading taken: yamabe's eq:sigma-bdry (sup of Y_[g], volume-normalized) and eq:gap-bdry with EH; EH = Y is proved here, so the two gaps agree. This bears more on T-perf-cor-yamabe.

kb_proposals: pattern: thm:main supplies lem:positivity for free. eq:main's F_g(1)/Λ_max is positive (Fq_one_pos, Λ_max ≥ β = 1), so upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos takes hpos from thm:main and nothing downstream of thm:main needs to carry lem:positivity or R_g ≤ 0 (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.lower_bound_of_eq_main).

pattern: a statement for one dimension whose constant is typed at N = 3 (star3_of_consts, Reads.thm_star3_corrected) can be stated at a generic N with (hN3 : N = 3) and `subst hN3` in the proof. The conclusion then reads exactly like the generic theorem's and needs no ((3 : ℕ) : ℝ) casts (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.thm_lower_bound_three, Mfd.Reads.thm_lower_bound_three).

pattern: to check that a scaffold module can graduate without name clashes, compile a /tmp copy of it with its imports replaced by `import Yamabe` (the whole strict root), under -DwarningAsError=true. This takes seconds and writes nothing.

convention: a topological invariant that is a supremum over conformal classes (σ^∂(Σ), σ(Σ̄)) is not definable on the model, because R and H are free data, so the supremum is unbounded and Real.sSup is junk 0. Carry it as a real parameter, state the sign-free form, and carry only the sign the paper's proof uses (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.gapBdry).
